chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, the seller of garments, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have considered leaving the marketplace, and in my hand is something (wealth/capital).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then your opinion (or status/standing) will be diminished, and people will not seek your counsel or assistance in anything.'

key_terms.رَأْيُكَ: Your opinion, judgment, or social standing

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social consequence of leaving trade while still holding wealth?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises a merchant not to withdraw from the market prematurely, warning that doing so while still holding capital will cause his 'opinion' (ray' - implying status, judgment, or professional standing) to fall into disuse. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on active participation in socio-economic life as a means of maintaining social utility and communal relevance, rather than seeking isolation. The advice underscores that professional engagement is not merely transactional but essential for preserving one's role and respect within the community.
